slides.kicker: AND HE MEANT IT AS AN INSULT
slides.image_prompt: Trump mocks Dario Amodei with bitter contempt, Dario's face sharply detailed and unmistakably recognizable, minimal background, Anthropic symbol, cutting mockery.

caption:
Trump called Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei a "perfect little angel" for wanting to slow down AI, and now no one will dare ask for a pause again.

Up until yesterday, even the fastest AI companies at least pretended to care about safety in public. Nobody wanted to be the executive on record saying "we don't care if this goes wrong."

Then Trump changed that. He looked at Dario Amodei, the CEO of Anthropic, one of the most powerful AI companies on Earth, and called him "pretending to be a perfect little angel" for wanting to slow things down. Out loud. As president. The official White House position on AI caution is now: it's an act.

Here's what makes it wild. Amodei didn't drift into this opinion. He quit his job at OpenAI specifically because he thought AI was already moving too fast, too dangerously. He then built Anthropic around that belief. Now the president is publicly calling him a fake for still believing it. The man who left to build safer AI just got mocked by the most powerful person on Earth for doing exactly that.

Every AI executive who watched this happen now knows the price of raising your hand and asking to slow down. So nobody will. You're now racing against a technology with no one left to ask for a pause. This is the moment AI safety stopped being a debate and became a punchline.

Every AI company watched. The US is officially flooring it on AI with no speed limit.

Running a business? DM us "AI" and we'll show you what an unregulated AI race means for yours.
